(US$2.4 billion) (2023) | net_income = {{down}} {{INR}} -158 crore
(US$ -19 million) (2023) | num_employees = 10,000+ (2021) | subsidiaries = {{plainlist| *[[Zee Media Corporation]] (4.34%) *[[Zee Entertainment Enterprises|Z Entertainment Enterprises Limited]] (3.99%) *[[Dish TV]] (4.04%) *[[Siti Networks]] (6.10%) }} | website = {{URL|http://www.esselgroup.com/}} | Broadcast Area = }} '''Essel Group''' (also known as '''Zee Group''') is an Indian [[media conglomerate]], headquartered in [[Mumbai]], India.{{Cite web|title=Tarun Katial {{!}} On the binge|url=https://www.livemint.com/mint-lounge/features/tarun-katial-on-the-binge-11580638681181.html|last=Sapam|first=Bidya|date=2020-02-02|website=[[Livemint]]|language=en}} The group has had business interests in [[mass media]], [[infrastructure]] and [[packaging]].{{Cite web|title=Sangh backs Zee in its fight for survival (IANS Exclusive)|url=https://www.outlookindia.com/newsscroll/sangh-backs-zee-in-its-fight-for-survival-ians-exclusive/1473656|date=6 February 2019|website=[[Outlook India]]}}{{Cite web|title=Essel Group in talks to raise $400 million to refinance debt|url=https://www.livemint.com/Companies/TVdcldqh0yIAWbEMLyTRkN/Essel-Group-in-talks-to-raise-400-million-to-refinance-debt.html|last=Chaki|first=Deborshi|date=2019-01-09|website=[[Livemint]]|language=en}}{{Cite web|title=India Inc's Crown Jewels At Risk- Business News|url=https://www.businesstoday.in/magazine/the-hub/india-inc-crown-jewels-at-risk/story/332850.html|last=Pratap|first=Rashmi|date=21 April 2019|website=[[Business Today (India)]]}} Founded in 1926 as the Messrs Ramgopal Indraprasad by Jagannath Goenka, the company was expanded and converted into the Essel Group of Industries by his grandson, [[Subhash Chandra]].{{Cite web|title=From 'Okara Dukaan' to Zee… the complete story|url=https://www.mxmindia.com/2012/10/from-okara-dukaan-to-zee-the-complete-story/|date=1 October 2012|website=MxMIndia}} Chandra is part of the Goenka (Goel) family which owns and operates the group; he was also the chairman of the company and a former member of the [[Rajya Sabha]].{{Cite news|title=Subhash Chandra and family|work=Media Ownership Monitor|publisher=[[Reporters Without Borders]]|url=http://india.mom-rsf.org/en/owners/individual-owners/detail/owner/owner/show/subhash-chandra-and-family/}} Experiencing financial troubles in 2019,{{Cite web|title=Subhash Chandra may lose say in Zee Entertainment|url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/subhash-chandra-may-lose-say-in-zee-entertainment-11572892358237.html|last1=Gopakumar|first1=Gopika|last2=Laskar|first2=Anirudh|date=2019-11-05|website=[[Livemint]]|language=en}}{{Cite web|date=15 April 2020|title=Sudhanshu Vats Appointed CEO And MD At Essel Propack|url=http://businessworld.in/article/Sudhanshu-Vats-Appointed-CEO-And-MD-At-Essel-Propack/15-04-2020-189298|website=[[BW Businessworld]]|language=en}} Essel sold off several of its assets, including [[Essel Propack]] and stakes in [[Zee Entertainment Enterprises]]. == History == === 1926–1967 === In 1926, Jagannath Goenka founded the Messrs Ramgopal Indraprasad as a commercial firm to deal in [[food grain]]s at the ''mandi'' ([[product market]]) in [[Adampur, Hisar]]. In 1946, as a result of poor performance in Adampur, the firm moved to the town of [[Hisar (city)|Hisar]]. Goenka attempted to expand the business in 1948 by setting up a [[Dal|pulses]] polishing factory in [[Delhi]], but he suffered heavy losses, forcing him to cease Delhi operations in 1951. He moved the Delhi machinery to Hisar, where he was able to turn consistent profits by selling polished [[whole grain]]s to [[Gujarat]] and [[South India]]. By 1966, the firm was operating one [[dal]] [[Mill (grinding)|mill]] and two [[cotton ginning]] factories.{{Primary source inline|date=May 2020}} === 1967–1992 === In 1967, the business suffered a series of losses, leaving the Goenka family at a net deficit of {{INRConvert|600,000||lk=on|year=1967}}. Between 1967–68, the Goenkas' connections in the [[Food Corporation of India]] (FCI) helped the family secure not only a deal to supply it with polished pulses and cleaned [[barley]] but also a later contract for storage of food grains. In 1973, control of the company was handed over to [[Subhash Chandra]], the grandson of Jagannath Goenka.{{Cite web|title=New Pastures For The Patriarch|url=http://businessworld.in/article/New-Pastures-For-The-Patriarch/08-11-2014-60132|last=Singh|first=Gurbir|date=8 November 2014|website=[[BW Businessworld]]|language=en|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181230131004/http://www.businessworld.in/article/New-Pastures-For-The-Patriarch/08-11-2014-60132/|archive-date=30 December 2018}} The company renamed itself the Essel Group in 1976. After acquiring a storage contract with the FCI in the same year, Essel established a new subsidiary, Lamina Packers, to manufacture packaging materials. In 1981, Essel obtained lucrative export contracts for rice and [[soya bean]]s as a result of Indo–[[USSR]] bilateral [[trade agreement]]s. According to a 2014 estimate, Essel Group's net worth by 1982 was over {{INRConvert|100|c|lk=on|year=2014}}. In December 1982, Lamina Packers became incorporated as [[Essel Packaging]], which marked Essel Group's full-blown venture into the [[packaging industry]], with the primary product being the laminated tube units that originated with Lamina Packers. In 1983, the group also began investing in a future amusement park in Mumbai. [[EsselWorld]] opened six years later, becoming India's first amusement park.{{Cite web|title=Subhash Chandra: interesting facts of chairman of the essel group|url=https://www.businessinsider.in/thelife/personalities/article/interesting-facts-about-chairman-of-the-essel-group-subash-chandra-that-will-inspire-many/articleshow/74171305.cms|date=17 October 2020|website=[[Business Insider]]}} Although the park was partly meant to signal that its parent corporation wanted to be a major force in the [[entertainment industry]], EsselWorld always remained unprofitable, right up to its shutdown in 2023.{{Cite web|title=Entertainment Inc.: The story of Zee, one of India's first Hindi {{sic|satel|ite|nolink=y}} channels|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/magazine/cover-story/story/20170821-zee-hindi-tv-channel-subhash-chandra-1028931-2017-08-11|last=Singh|first=Suhani|date=21 August 2017|website=[[India Today]]|language=en|access-date=2020-02-26}}{{Cite web|title=Subhash Chandra makes television history with Zee TV began life running a flour-mill|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/magazine/profile/story/19940815-subhash-chandra-makes-television-history-with-zee-tv-began-life-running-a-flour-mill-809511-1994-08-15|last=Agarwal|first=Amit|date=12 July 2013|website=India Today|language=en|publication-date=15 August 1994|access-date=28 February 2020}} === 1992–Present === As of 1992, Essel Group began to take a bigger interest and stake in the entertainment industry. That year it incorporated [[Zee Telefilms|Zee Telefilms Ltd]]{{Cite web|title=Zee Entertainment Enterprises History|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/zee-entertainment-enterprises-ltd/infocompanyhistory/companyid-11769.cms|website=[[The Economic Times]]|access-date=2020-02-26}} and then looked for a place where Zee's content could be broadcast. Zee and [[Star TV (Asian TV networks)|Star TV]] entered into a joint venture called Asia Today Ltd so Zee could lease a [[transponder]] from satellite network [[AsiaSat]]. The transponder agreement was signed in April 1992, and [[Zee TV]] began broadcasting on 1 October.{{Cite web|title=There and back again: Subhash Chandra and the Zee TV story|url=https://www.livemint.com/Companies/DY6tYikVelf4mtIywJh6eN/There-and-back-again-Subhash-Chandra-and-the-Zee-TV-story.html|last1=Bansal|first1=Shuchi|last2=Sheikh|first2=Aminah|date=2012-09-29|website=[[Livemint]]|language=en|access-date=2020-02-26}} It was India's first [[Hindi Language]] satellite channel, and by 1994 it had captured 65% of the satellite market share. Zee TV remained the [[market leader]] until 2000. In 1994,{{Cite web|title=Siti Networks|url=http://www.sitinetworks.com/|website=sitinetworks.com|language=en|access-date=2020-05-12}} Essel Group incorporated [[Siti Cable]] to be the [[Distribution (marketing)|distribution]] subsidiary of Zee Telefilms. Siti would provide [[cable service]] to customers to expand the reach of Zee's satellite channels. The company continued to develop entertainment channels that successfully competed with [[Star India]], a Star TV subsidiary. In 1998, Essel/Zee turned to journalism with [[Zee News]], the first 24x7 [[Hindi Language]] news channel in India.{{Cite book|title=The Politics of Sport in South Asia|publisher=[[Routledge]]|year=2010|isbn=978-0-415-37168-1|editor-last=Chakraborty|editor-first=Subhas Ranjan|location=[[Oxfordshire]] & [[New York City|New York]]|pages=136|editor-last2=Chakrabarti|editor-first2=Shantanu|editor-last3=Chaterjee|editor-first3=Kingshuk}} In 2000, Zee Telefilms ended its partnership with Star TV by [[buyout|buying out]] its shares in Asia Today Ltd. October 2021 |language=en}} === Dish TV (4.04% stake) === {{main|Dish TV}} '''DishTV India Limited''' (abbreviated as '''DTIL''', stylised as '''dishtv''') is a [[Direct to Home]] (DTH) television Dish TV was launched on 2 October 2003 as the DTH provider of the Essel Group and was merged with [[Videocon D2H]] on 22 March 2018.{{Cite news|last=Das Gupta|first=Surajeet|date=2014-01-01|title=10 years of DTH in India: The other electronics revolution|work=[[Business Standard India]]|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/10-years-of-dth-in-india-the-other-electronics-revolution-114010100022_1.html}}{{cite web|title=Dish TV India, Videocon d2h merger completed|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/media/entertainment/media/dish-tv-india-videocon-d2h-merger-completed/articleshow/63414778.cms|date=22 March 2018|website=The Economic Times}} The Essel Group maintains a 55% stake in the company while the [[Videocon Group]] maintains a 45% stake.{{Cite web|title=Dish TV and Videocon d2h merger gets CCI approval|url=https://www.livemint.com/Companies/FULbZN0PRVxgPcBVeI0nEN/Dish-TV-and-Videocond2h-merger-gets-CCI-approval.html|last=Ahluwalia|first=Harveen|date=2017-05-10|website=[[Livemint]]|language=en}} It became the largest DTH provider in India after the merger. The company is also partnered with [[The Times Group]] owned [[MX Player]] for [[streaming service]]s. In May 2021, it was reported that promoters' shareholding in [[Dish TV]] has fallen to just 5.67% and [[Yes Bank]] has become biggest stock owner of [[Dish TV]].{{Cite news|title=Dish TV promoters' stake falls to 5.67%|work=The Economic Times|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/dish-tv-promoters-stake-falls-to-5-67/articleshow/82749888.cms?from=mdr|access-date=2021-10-10}} The shareholding further fell to 4.04% by 2023. === Zee Entertainment Enterprises (3.99% stake) === {{main|Zee Entertainment Enterprises}} The '''Zee Entertainment Enterprises Limited''' (abbreviated as '''ZEEL'''; formerly '''Zee Telefilms Limited''') is a media and [[entertainment]] broadcasting company.{{Cite news|date=2020-04-23|title=ZEEL jumps after foreign fund buys stake|work=[[Business Standard India]]|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/news-cm/zeel-jumps-after-foreign-fund-buys-stake-120042300468_1.html}} It was the primary profit generating company of the Essel Group.{{Cite web|title=Why Subash Chandra had to Resign as Chairman of Zee|url=https://www.newsclick.in/Subhash-Chandra-Zee-Chairman-Resings-Essel-Group|date=2019-11-27|website=NewsClick|language=en}} It owns a constellation of [[entertainment]] channels under the brand name of ''Zee'' and the channels under the brands of ''Living Entertainment'', ''Big'' and "&".List of sources: *{{Cite web|title=Zee to launch movie channel under new brand '& pictures'|url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/Zee-to-launch-movie-channel-under-new-brand-%E2%80%98amp-pictures%E2%80%99/article20646185.ece|date=8 August 2013|website=[[Business Line]]|language=en|access-date=2020-02-26}} *{{Cite web|title=ZEE Entertainment launches new Hindi General Entertainment Channel '&TV' - Times of India|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/tv/news/hindi/ZEE-Entertainment-launches-new-Hindi-General-Entertainment-Channel-TV/articleshow/45974989.cms|date=22 January 2015|website=[[The Times of India]]|language=en|access-date=2020-02-26}} *{{Cite news|last=Malvania|first=Urvi|date=2015-09-03|title=Essel launches Living Foodz|work=[[Business Standard]]|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/management/essel-launches-living-foodz-115090301284_1.html|access-date=2020-02-26}} *{{Cite web|title=ZEE Acquires Anil Ambani-led Regional Channels Big Magic, Big Ganga|url=http://businessworld.in/article/ZEE-Acquires-Anil-Ambani-led-Regional-Channels-Big-Magic-Big-Ganga/23-11-2016-108712|last=Hasan|first=Abid|date=23 November 2016|website=[[Businessworld]]|language=en|access-date=2020-02-27}} The Zee Entertainment Enterprise also owns and operates the [[record label]] of [[Zee Music Company]] and the [[film studio]] of [[Zee Studios]].List of sources: * *{{Cite web|title=Zee Music Company Teams Up With Sony Music Entertainment|url=https://businessofcinema.com/business/zee-music-company-teams-sony-music-entertainment/141781|date=2014-04-18|website=Business of Cinema|language=en-US}} *{{Cite web|title=Zee to re-enter film production|url=https://www.livemint.com/Companies/9LPq0UoLCVAnpzcKeqfeNL/Zee-to-reenter-film-production.html|last=K.K|first=Sruthijith|date=2008-06-19|website=[[Livemint]]|language=en}} *{{cite news|year=2008|title=Zee Group launches two motion picture production banners|publisher=Business of Cinema|url=https://businessofcinema.com/bollywood-news/zee-group-launches-two-motion-picture-production-banners/22232}} * The company was incorporated in 1992 as the Zee Telefilms Limited, the Essel Group's venture into [[mass media]]. It launched its flagship television channel, Zee TV on 1 October 1992. In 2006, two subsidiaries of the company were de-merged from the Zee Telefilms Ltd and segregated as distinct ententes under the Essel Group. Zee News Ltd (later renamed to Zee Media Corporation) became the news broadcasting subsidiary of the group while Wire & Wireless India Limited (later renamed to [[Siti Networks]]) became the [[Cable television|cable distribution]] company of the group. Following the segregation, Zee Telefilms was rebranded as to Zee Entertainment Enterprises. Between 2002–2018, the Zee Entertainment Enterprises was involved a joint venture with american distribution brand [[Turner India]] for the distribution of channels in India, [[Nepal]] and [[Bhutan]].{{Cite web|title=Turner International appoints IndiaCast Media as its distribution agent|url=https://www.livemint.com/Consumer/D1xzMQSdejCUExSXGbbUdL/Turner-International-appoints-IndiaCast-Media-as-its-distrib.html|last=Jha|first=Lata|date=2018-03-27|website=[[Livemint]]|language=en}} The company was involved in sports broadcasting between 2004–2016. It launched its own private cricket league, the [[Indian Cricket League]] which held two seasons between 2007–2009 but the league failed to gain traction.{{Cite book|last1=Evens|first1=Tom|title=The Political Economy of Television Sports Rights|last2=Isifidis|first2=Petros|last3=Smith|first3=Paul|publisher=[[Palgrave Macmillan]]|year=2013|isbn=978-1-137-27564-6|pages=152–158}} In 2016, it sold off all its sports broadcasting assets in the venture to [[Sony]].{{Cite news|last=Malvania|first=Urvi|date=2016-09-01|title=ZEE sells Ten Sports to Sony for $385 mn|work=[[Business Standard India]]|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/zee-sells-ten-sports-to-sony-for-385-mn-116083100446_1.html}} As of 2020, the company has suffered successive reduction in revenue and has been subjected to investigative probes by the [[Enforcement Directorate]].{{Cite news|last=Pinto|first=Viveat Susan|date=2020-03-18|title=Zee Entertainment stock falls 20% a day after ED summons Subhash Chandra|work=[[Business Standard India]]|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/zee-entertainment-stock-falls-20-a-day-after-ed-summons-subhash-chandra-120031800032_1.html}}{{Cite web|title=Corporate Governance: Corp affairs ministry probes Zee Entertainment's books|url=https://www.financialexpress.com/industry/corporate-governance-corp-affairs-ministry-probes-zee-entertainments-books/1857906/|date=2020-02-06|website=[[The Financial Express (India)|The Financial Express]]|language=en-US}} The Essel Group has divested a part of its shares in the company for the repayment of pending dues, reducing its stake in the company to 22.37% with much of the remaining stake still pledged as collateral to the remaining dues. In September 2021 ZEEL Announced merger with [[Sony Pictures Networks India]]. In October 2021, it was reported that founder [[Subhash Chandra]] and his son, [[Punit Goenka]] together own just 3.99% stake of [[Zee Entertainment]].{{Cite web|last=Sood|first=Varun|date=2021-09-30|title=Tribunal orders Zee to announce EGM by Sunday|url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/tribunal-orders-zee-to-announce-egm-by-sunday-11633025364422.html|access-date=2021-10-10|website=mint|language=en}} On 22 December the board of [[Zee Entertainment Enterprises]] approved the merger with [[Sony Pictures Networks India]]. and now pending for government approval. === Zee Learn (15.05% stake) === The '''Zee Learn Limited''' (abbreviated as '''ZLL'''; informally referred to as '''Zee Schools''') is the [[for-profit education]] company of the Essel Group.{{Cite web |date=9 April 2010 |title=Essel Group bets big on education |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/todays-paper/tp-marketing/Essel-Group-bets-big-on-education/article20042725.ece |website=[[Business Line]] |language=en}} Incorporated in 1958, the company did not begin operating until 2010.{{Cite web |title=Zee Learn History |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/zee-learn-ltd/infocompanyhistory/companyid-32769.cms |website=[[The Economic Times]]}} Zee Learn founded the [[private school]] chains of Kidzee [[preschool]]s and Mount Litera Zee [[K–12]] schools. As of 2019, it had more than 1,900 Kidzee preschools and 120 Mount Litera Zee schools across India and three [[institutes of higher education]]; the Zee Institute of Media Arts (ZIMA), Zee Institute of Creative Arts (ZICA) and the Himgiri Zee University, Dehradun (HZU). The company also promoted and operated he [[ZeeQ]] channel of the Zee Entertainment Enterprises.{{cite web |date=15 October 2012 |title=Zee launches kids edutainment channel ZeeQ |url=http://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/zee-launches-kids-edutainment-channel-zeeq-112101500137_1.html |work=[[Business Standard India]]}} The student [[coaching]] firm MT Educare became a subsidiary of Zee Learn following an acquisition in May 2018.{{Cite web |last=Saraswathy |first=M |date=5 May 2020 |title=Zee Learn dismisses scepticism over MT Educare buy, says working to expand product, brand reach |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/companies/zee-learn-dismisses-scepticism-over-mt-educare-buy-says-working-to-expand-product-brand-reach-5224071.html |website=[[Moneycontrol]]}} It has been inactive since 2020 and has become a direct subsidiary of Zee Entertainment Enterprises despite having a separate stock listing. === Others === The group owned and operated [[amusement park]]s of "Essel World" and "Water Kingdom" in [[Mumbai]].{{Cite news|last=Menon|first=Shailesh|date=2018-02-06|title=Meet the first families of the growing theme and amusement parks segment in India|work=[[The Economic Times]]|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/company/corporate-trends/meet-the-first-families-of-the-growing-theme-and-amusement-parks-segment-in-india/articleshow/62795406.cms}} Essel World was one of the first amusement parks in India; it was shut down in April 2023.{{Cite web |date=2023-05-04 |title=Mumbai: Essel World Shut Down? Heartbroken 90s, Early 2000s Kids Take Nostalgia Trip on Twitter |url=https://www.timesnownews.com/mumbai/mumbai-essel-world-shut-down-heartbroken-90s-early-2000s-kids-take-nostalgia-trip-on-twitter-article-99986954 |access-date=2023-05-07 |website=TimesNow |language=en}} The [[Shirpur Gold Refinery]] uses the brand name of ''Zee Gold'' in a joint venture with the Essel Group for the marketing of the refinery's products; the Essel Group gets royalties of 20% on the net profit for the brand usage.{{Cite news|title=Shirpur Gold Refinery Ltd.|work=[[Business Standard India]]|url=https://www.business-standard.com/company/shirpur-gold-18695/information/company-history}} The Refinery recently went public diluting Essel Group's stake to 43.66%.{{Cite web |title=Shirpur Gold Share Price, Shirpur Gold Stock Price, Shirpur Gold Refinery Ltd. Stock Price, Share Price, Live BSE/NSE, Shirpur Gold Refinery Ltd. Bids Offers. Buy/Sell Shirpur Gold Refinery Ltd. news & tips, & F&O Quotes, NSE/BSE Forecast News and Live Quotes |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/india/stockpricequote/miningminerals/shirpurgoldrefinery/AGR |access-date=2023-05-07 |website=www.moneycontrol.com |language=en |last1=Com |first1=Moneycontrol }} The group also operated the online [[lottery]] Playwin in [[Sikkim]].{{Cite web|last=Shangderpa|first=Pema Leyda|date=22 August 2003|title=Appeal in SC for Playwin|url=https://www.telegraphindia.com/west-bengal/appeal-in-sc-for-playwin/cid/808811|website=[[The Telegraph (Calcutta)]]|language=en}} The lottery however ceased operation in 2020, following the sale of assets by the Essel Group for the repayment of pending debts.{{Cite news|date=2019-09-07|title=Essel Group repays half the debt to MFs & NBFCs|work=[[The Economic Times]]|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/essel-repays-half-the-debt-to-mfs-nbfcs/articleshow/71020215.cms}} Essel Group had founded and operated [[Essel Propack]] until sale of their stake in 2019. Between 2020 and 2021, Essel Group sold Essel Finance's MSME loan book to [[Adani Group|Adani Capital]],{{cite news |title=Essel Group sells MSME loan book to Adani Capital |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/essel-group-sells-msme-loan-book-to-adani-capital/articleshow/73525605.cms |access-date=24 November 2024 |work=The Times of India |date=22 January 2020}} and Essel Mutual Fund to [[Navi Group]].{{cite news |last1=Pillai |first1=Anvita |title=Sachin Bansal's Navi Mutual Fund Files Papers For Electric Vehicle Fund With SEBI |url=https://inc42.com/buzz/sachin-bansals-navi-mutual-fund-files-papers-for-ev-fund-with-sebi/ |access-date=24 November 2024 |work=Inc42 Media |date=18 September 2021 |language=en}} == Controversy == === Zee Entertainment Enterprises Limited (Dispute between Promoters) === On 11 September 2021, Invesco asked Zee management to call an "extraordinary general meeting" (EGM) of shareholders to consider its demands. One of the main demands was the removal of [[Punit Goenka]], son of the Zee Network founder.{{Cite web|title=Zee Entertainment's Largest Shareholders Call EGM Seeking Removal Of Punit Goenka From September 2021 |language=en}} However the Zee board rejected the demand from Invesco to convene an extraordinary general meeting.{{Cite web|title=Zee Says Will Not Hold EGM As Demanded By Shareholder On 11 October 2021, [[Invesco]]{{Cite web|title=Invesco Shoots Letter To Zee Shareholders, Seeks Better Governance, Says Founding Family Benefiting At The Cost Of Others|url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/companies/disappointed-that-leadership-of-zee-has-resorted-to-reckless-public-relations-campaign-invesco-mf-to-shareholders-7569571.html|access-date=2021-10-21|website=Moneycontrol|date=11 October 2021 |language=en}} wrote an open letter to the other shareholders saying they are disappointed that the leadership of Zee has resorted to a reckless public relations campaign in response to the overwhelming demand from shareholders for leadership changes at Zee network. They had also tried to merge Zee with some other Indian company in early 2021, but the Zee board rejected it. The Zee Board replied to Invesco's open letter saying they didn't care about the company, and Invesco is not motivated by concerns related to any corporate governance issue,{{Cite web|title=Zee Hits Back At Invesco's Open Letter, Rebuts Objections On Sony Merger Deal|url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/companies/zee-hits-back-at-invescos-open-letter-rebuts-objections-on-sony-merger-deal-7579641.html|access-date=2021-10-21|website=Moneycontrol|date=13 October 2021 |language=en}} but "by the events that transpired during February-April 2021 pointing Invesco purposed deal with [[Reliance Industries]].{{Cite web|title=Invesco Proposed Merger With Large Indian Group In Feb 2021, Wanted Punit Goenka To Lead: Zee|url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/companies/invesco-proposed-merger-with-large-indian-group-in-feb-2021-wanted-punit-goenka-to-lead-zee-7575661.html|access-date=2021-10-21|website=Moneycontrol|date=12 October 2021 |language=en}} Reliance Industries Ltd (RIL) said it proposed to merge all its media properties with Zee Entertainment at fair valuations during discussions in February and March 2021 that US investment firm Invesco helped arrange with managing director and member of the founding family of the media and entertainment company. extract:
Essel Group (also known as Zee Group) is an Indian media conglomerate, headquartered in Mumbai, India. The group has had business interests in mass media, infrastructure and packaging. Founded in 1926 as the Messrs Ramgopal Indraprasad by Jagannath Goenka, the company was expanded and converted into the Essel Group of Industries by his grandson, Subhash Chandra. 
Chandra is part of the Goenka (Goel) family which owns and operates the group; he was also the chairman of the company and a former member of the Rajya Sabha.
Experiencing financial troubles in 2019, Essel sold off several of its assets, including Essel Propack and stakes in Zee Entertainment Enterprises.
